To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the upgrading potential of nascent geographical indication (GI) systems, as applied to small-scale producers in developing countries, has been under-researched.

the case of the Makó onion PDO shows that the potential of geographical indications to facilitate upgrading is limited in the context of nascent PDO systems, and that the reasons for this are related to the institutional context.

(a) the Makó Onion PDO has failed to deliver any upgrading benefits to its small-scale producers and (b) the failure to deliver upgrading benefits can be attributed to a lack of collective action and the inability of producers to capture higher margins, both of which can be attributed to the political context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which a nascent geographical indication system (the Makó onion PDO, Hungary) can contribute to the upgrading of small-scale onion producers.

the question of how to improve the positioning of marginalised small-scale producers in the global agro-food system, with the potential to contribute to debates on the role of geographical indications in this context.
the role of geographical indications as a tool for improving the positioning of small scale producers in global agri-food chains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Makó onion PDO is not an effective tool to upgrade the value chain of small-scale onion producers.
geographical indications do not necessarily improve the position of small-scale producers, and may not be the panacea that they have been made out to be.
, although geographical indications may have the potential to improve the positioning of producers, this is not guaranteed, and in the context of nascent systems, the potential is not realised.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
geographical indications are a powerful tool to improve the position of small-scale producers and their communities.
, while there is no doubt that GIs can help producers, there are also many cases when they do not.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, for nascent geographical indication to have a chance to succeed, it is necessary that the political and institutional environment is supportive.

the benefits from geographical indications for smallholders are limited, and that the potential for geographical indications to improve the position of smallholders is highly dependent on the institutional context.

geographical indications may be an effective tool for facilitating the upgrading of small-scale farmers, but only if the political and institutional contexts in which they are implemented are supportive.
